result.summary:
TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independent re-verification of REQ-168's MemoryGuard test suite (commit 69f021e, 18 tests) -- PASS. Read the implementation (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex, 170 lines), the full test file (test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs, 262 lines), TEST-DESIGNER's full report, and REQ-168's acceptance_criteria in docs/requirements.yaml directly; did not trust the prior report's claims without independent reproduction.

AC MAPPING (all 6 of REQ-168's real acceptance_criteria have runnable, passing coverage):
1. Single validation function / repo-search: independently re-ran `grep -rn 'Wasmex\.Memory\.' lib/ --include='*.ex'` myself -- every hit is inside memory_guard.ex (size/2, read_binary/4, write_binary/4 only); no other guest-memory read/write path exists in lib/. Confirms AC1.
2. Malformed pointer -> structured error, BEAM node/process stay up: T3 describe block, 4 tests, each asserting `Process.alive?(self())` and the PluginTaskSupervisor is alive after a malformed read/4 or write/4 call. Confirms AC2.
3. Offset beyond size / length past end / offset+length overflow, each rejected before dereference: T2 describe block covers all three named shapes plus extra defensive cases (negative offset, non-integer length) -- all against pure check_bounds/3. Confirms AC3.
4. Two instances don't share memory: T4's single test writes <<99>> in instance A, reads 0 from instance B at the same offset, and confirms A still reads its own write. Confirms AC4.
5. Moduledoc discloses the Wasmtime-native residual-risk boundary consistent with REQ-165: T5, two tests (generic phrase-match plus a stricter citation/quote match on req165 section 7.2). Confirms AC5.
6. mix test / mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass: both re-run myself, see below. Confirms AC6.

No `@tag :skip`, no 'TODO: implement test', no pending tests anywhere in memory_guard_test.exs or test/specs/REQ-168.md (grep for skip/TODO/pending returned nothing). No hardcoded secrets/connection strings (grep for password/secret/api_key/token returned nothing). Tests are self-sufficient: each test in T1-T5 calls its own `start_instance()` or uses only its own literal arguments to check_bounds/3 -- no shared mutable fixture state, no test depends on another having run first (module is `async: false` for the documented NIF-serialization reason, not for cross-test data dependency).

INDEPENDENT MUTATION RE-VERIFICATION (both genuinely-new-gap mutants reproduced myself from a clean baseline, not copied from the report):

Baseline: `mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs` (with `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"` and `WASMEX_BUILD=true`) -- Result: 18 passed, 0 failed.

Mutant 1 (64-bit-truncation on check_end_of_range/3): edited `range_end = offset + length` to `range_end = Bitwise.band(offset + length, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)`. Ran the suite: Result: 17/18 passed, 1 failed -- exactly the new 2^64-magnitude test ('end-of-range sum chosen so a truncated-to-64-bit accumulator would wrap to zero...'), with `left: :ok, right: {:error, {:length_exceeds_memory, 0, 18446744073709551616, 65536}}`, matching the reported false-accept mechanism precisely. Reverted with `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex`; confirmed `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty and re-ran suite: 18 passed again.

Mutant 2 (write/4 hardcoded length): edited `length = byte_size(data)` to `length = 1`. Ran the suite: Result: 17/18 passed, 1 failed -- exactly the new write/4 length-confusion test, with `left: {:error, {:invalid_pointer, {:memory_access_failed, "out of bounds memory access"}}}, right: {:error, {:invalid_pointer, {:length_exceeds_memory, 65531, 10, 65536}}}`, matching the reported wasmex-native-fallback-vs-clean-rejection mismatch precisely. Reverted with `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex`; confirmed `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty and re-ran suite: 18 passed again.

Both mutants were applied and reverted in the working tree directly (not a separate worktree); the revert was verified in both cases via an empty `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` AND a green re-run of the test file before proceeding, per this role's mandatory revert-and-verify discipline.

CRITICAL SAFETY CHECK (magnitude audit, performed personally by reading every literal argument in the file): read all 18 test cases' exact code. Every call to `check_bounds/3` with an extreme magnitude (offset=length=2^63 in T2 case 3; offset=0,length=2^63 in T2 case 4; offset=0,length=2^64 in T2 case 5) is a pure-function call with zero Wasmex/NIF dependency -- confirmed by reading check_bounds/3's own definition, which takes only plain integers and does no NIF call. Every live call to `read/4` or `write/4` (all in T3 and T4) uses only small/moderate literal magnitudes: 0, 1, 2, 10, size+1000, size-1, size-5, size+1, 1000, <<99>>, "hi", "x", and a 10-byte binary -- none within many orders of magnitude of 2^40 (~1.1e12); the largest live-call magnitude anywhere in the file is `size + 1000` (~66536). No direct `Wasmex.Memory.*` call appears anywhere in the test file outside of `Wasmex.Memory.size/2` (used only to read the real memory size, never to pass an attacker-controlled magnitude) -- confirmed via `grep -n 'Wasmex\.Memory\.' test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs`. No test, existing or new, ever calls a live Wasmex.Memory function at or above 2^40. This is confirmed independently, not copied from TEST-DESIGNER's claim.

The new 2^64-magnitude test case (test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs:102-120) was read in full: it calls `MemoryGuard.check_bounds(offset, length, 65536)` only -- no `start_instance()`, no `store`/`memory` handle, no `read/4`/`write/4`/`Wasmex.Memory.*` call anywhere in that test. Confirmed pure-function-only.

FINAL VERIFICATION RUN: `mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs` -- Result: 18 passed, 0 failed (seed 12245/238043/823140 across the several runs performed, all green on the unmutated implementation). `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- clean, no output, exit success. `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` -- empty (no leftover mutant state).

No coverage gap, no overclaim, and no safety-constraint violation found. TEST-DESIGNER's report is corroborated by independent reproduction on every claim checked.
